subject: URGENT: Peak Retail live SDK mis-parse causing throughput collapse during peak window
body:
From: Sally Wu <sally.wu@peakretail.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: infra@peakretail.com
Date: 2029-05-11T07:22:00Z
Subject: Re: LiveStream feed errors during morning peak

Ben —

We started to see a sharp drop in throughput and a spike to ~12% 5xx errors on the LiveStream endpoint at 07:10 UTC. This lasted ~18 minutes and impacted several storefronts during our morning flash sale. Attached is the partial capture from our load balancer and a short log from the client side (peak_retail_livestream.log).

Most errors show as 502/503 with brief connect resets, and our SDK clients reported repeated "stream decode timeout" errors. This looks related to the new 2.1.0 LiveStream SDK we onboarded last week. Can your team confirm whether there were any infra or rollout events on your side? We need a timeline and root cause ASAP — this hit our SLA and generated escalations to our CIO.

—Sally
Sally Wu
Head of Platform
Peak Retail

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Sally Wu <sally.wu@peakretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-05-11T07:35:00Z
Subject: Re: LiveStream feed errors during morning peak

Sally — thank you for the quick heads up and the logs. I'm escalating internally and copying our on-call infra and SDK leads. We have no planned deploys in that window.

Next steps:
- I have opened INF-4821 and attached the logs you provided.
- Marissa, Karthik — can you triage the attach and confirm whether this matches any codec/runtime anomalies?
- I'll schedule an urgent bridge with Peak Infra in 30 minutes unless you prefer otherwise.

We understand the SLA impact and will prioritize.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0117

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-05-11T07:48:00Z
Subject: Re: LiveStream feed errors during morning peak

Ben / team — I pulled the LB capture and the SDK dump. Initial observation: a subset of client connections terminated with truncated header frames followed by a parser error in the SDK that manifests as a "decode timeout" and then a 5xx from our fronting gateway.

Details:
- The SDK runtime shows repeated partial header boundaries where the trailing delimiter "\r\n\r\n" is missing for fragments ~1.2–2.8% of requests at very high concurrency.
- Our gateway treats these as malformed streams and returns a 502; the SDK treats the stream as stalled and retries, amplifying load.
- This pattern lines up with the customer timeframe and their reported error codes.

I need Karthik and Priyom to validate whether this is an SDK parser regression (2.1.0) vs. an upstream transport edge case. If it's the SDK, we should prepare an immediate patch and a downgrade path for Peak.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Reliability
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

---

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-05-11T08:15:00Z
Subject: Re: LiveStream feed errors during morning peak

Quick triage results:
- Reproduced locally under a synthetic stress runner that mimics Peak's client concurrency. The SDK streaming parser in 2.1.0 incorrectly assumes single-chunk header delivery in the fast-path; when header bytes are split across TCP segments it fails to assemble the delimiter in time and raises a parse exception.
- Root cause: an optimization introduced to reduce allocations merged header scanning; it skipped the reassembly codepath for multi-segment headers. Under very high concurrency and small MTU shapes (their mobile clients), the condition is hit more often.

Action items (immediate):
1) Prepare emergency 2.1.1 hotfix reverting the fast-path optimization (Priyom).
2) For Peak Retail: propose rollback to 2.0.8 and apply a temporary gateway retry-backoff to avoid amplification.
3) Ops: rate-limit retry storms from client IPs for 30 minutes to reduce load while we fix.

I'll push a proof-of-fix binary and a short test harness to INF-4821.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment(s): sdk_dump_20290511.json

---

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Sally Wu <sally.wu@peakretail.com>, infra@peakretail.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-05-11T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: LiveStream feed errors during morning peak

Sally — update from our engineering team: we've identified a client SDK parser regression in the 2.1.0 release that can fail when header bytes are split across TCP segments on high-concurrency mobile workloads. Karthik is producing a hotfix (2.1.1) and we strongly recommend rolling back to 2.0.8 now to stop the immediate SLA impact.

We can do the rollback for you if you want — or provide a pinned dependency and a step-by-step. We will also push a gateway configuration change to reduce retry amplification while we validate the fix.

Can you confirm whether you want Redwood to execute the rollback (we'd request short maintenance notification) or if Peak prefers to handle it? We can have the hotfix out within ~2 hours and a tested patch in ~4 hours.

Ben

From: Sally Wu <sally.wu@peakretail.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: LiveStream feed errors during morning peak

Ben — thanks for the rapid response and the clear RCA. Please proceed with the rollback for our fleet; we don't have time to stage it safely across thousands of mobile clients. Please coordinate the maintenance window with infra@peakretail.com. Also loop in your exec sponsor — this reached our CIO and we'd like a short postmortem for our board.

I'll wait for the rollback ETA and the hotfix timeline. We appreciate the prioritization.

—Sally
